items.title: ‘Only demanding our safety on campus’: SRFTI students’ union vice president on FIR after rustication
items.summary: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata has filed a case against students’ union vice president Shubham Waydande for allegedly assaulting its vice chancellor. Waydande is one of six students the institute rusticated on October 15. He was rusticated for three semesters, while the other five were rusticated for two semesters each. The campus has remained tense for the past month. It all began on September 27, when students protested an event on campus organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, a body affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Students and organisers clashed. On October 4, a large crowd from outside gathered at the institute’s gate and shouted slogans. There were also reports of stone-pelting and injured students. SRFTI clarifies that disciplinary action against certain students stems from specific acts of misconduct, including vandalism, defacement, and physical assault—not peaceful protest. The Institute upholds the right to peaceful dissent while ensuring accountability under its rules. #SRFTI #PressRelease #DisciplinaryAction #StudentSafety — Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (@srfti_official) October 25, 2026 Student

The Court observed that Khan and his son had already served substantial portions of their fixed-term sentences. items.title: Collegium recommends appointment of 5 judicial officers as Madhya Pradesh High Court judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Friday recommended the appointment of five judicial officers as judges of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The judicial officers recommended for elevation are: - Renuka Kanchan; - Krishnamurty Mishra; - Virendra Singh Rajput; - Mamta Jain; - Ashita Shrivastava. The Collegium had also recommended the appointment of seven advocates as judges of the High Court on October 26. The Collegium's recommendations will now be forwarded to the Central government for further processing. The appointments will take effect once the Central government clears the recommendations and the President of India issues the necessary warrants of appointment. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has a sanctioned strength of 53 judges. As of September 2026, the High Court had 38 serving judges against a sanctioned strength of 53, leaving 15 vacancies. items.title: Supreme Court to vet RBI’s digital fraud regulations before notification, says banks must compensate victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI’s) proposed anti-cyber fraud regulations before they are notified. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning digital arrest scams. The case arose from a senior citizen couple’s complaint of losing ₹1.05 crore to impersonators using forged judicial orders. It said that the regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where fraud results from failed due diligence. Compensation must be at least equivalent to the customer’s loss, the Court said. “The amount will remain intact. The bank will have to pay. That is the only way,” the CJI remarked, stressing that liability could not stop with individual officers. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Justice Bagchi questioned why financial institutions should not face strict liability when their failure to provide safeguards enables misuse of banking products. items.summary: A Gujarat court recently cited Hindu scriptures, including the Manusmriti and the Rigveda, while sentencing three men to life imprisonment for cow slaughter. Justice Brijeshkumari Rameshwarsinh Rajput , presiding over the Third Additional Sessions Court in Gandhinagar's Kalol held that cows could become extinct if people who slaughter them are not punished in accordance with the law. "આવા આરોપીઓ કે જઓએ અ ે તિક્રુરતા પુર્વક ગાયોના અંશો કાપી કાપીને અલગ કરી નાખેલાં તેવા આરોપીઓને કાયદામાં પ્રસ્થાપિત ;HF કરવામાં ન આવે તો સમય જતાં ધરતી ઉપર ગાૈમાતા લુપ્ત થઇ જશે માટે આરોપીઓને કાયદામાં પ્રસ્થાિપ્ત પ્રમાણેની સજા કરવી જરૂરી જણાઇ આવતી હોય નીચે મુજબનો આખરી હુકમ કરવામાં આવે છે," the Court said in its judgment dated October 26. (translation) "If accused persons such as these, who have cruelly cut the body parts of cows into pieces and separated them, are not punished in accordance with the law, then, over time, Gau Mata will become extinct from the earth. Therefore, it is considered necessary to sentence the accused in accordance with the law, and the following final order is passed." items.title: From appetite to austerity: Health underwriting under the DPDP regime
items.summary: The notification of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, and the subsequent Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, mark a tectonic shift in India’s privacy jurisprudence. The Act's implementation in the health insurance sector exposes a striking structural tension. The industry’s core model, which relies on exhaustive disclosures at various stages, now has to be reconciled with a legal framework that demands a much narrower, purpose-specific approach to data. At the heart of this conflict lie two cardinal principles of data protection: data minimisation and purpose limitation. For an industry where more data traditionally equals fair risk pricing and coverage sustainability, the DPDP Act’s imposition of data minimization and purpose limitation demands a radical contraction of data appetites. items.title: Holy cow, unholy sentence
items.summary: In a secular constitutional republic, criminal courts are tasked with measuring guilt against the penal code, weighing evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and sentencing offenders within the rational bounds of statutory discretion. On October 26, an additional sessions court at Kalol in Gandhinagar district of Gujarat chose a rather different source of jurisprudence. Judge Brijeshkumari Rameshwarsinh Rajput sentenced three men - Wasim, Mohammed Rafiq and Ashfaq - to rigorous imprisonment for life based on the recovery of 277 kilograms of beef, seized during a raid on a village house in Jamla. To justify locking three men in prison until their natural death, the court found standard principles of proportionality, penology, or individual reformation as petty distractions - far too mundane for the case in hand. Instead, the judgment embarked on an expansive theological excursion. Drawing directly from the Rigveda , the Manusmriti and the Harivamsa Purana , the court noted that the cow houses 33 crore deities; that the sun and moon dwell within its eyes; that Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh inhabit its horns; and that the four legs of the bovine represent the four Vedas. items.title: Kerala High Court upholds relief to Wipro over 'Brahmins' sambar powder trademark
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld the temporary injunction imposed on Greenmount Spices, restricting it from using the ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks until a trademark infringement suit filed by Wipro Enterprises is decided. [ Greenmount Spices Private Limited v. Wipro Enterprises Private Limited ] Justice CS Dias opined that Wipro had established a prima facie case to support its claim of prior commercial use of the trademarks in question. " I am satisfied that the respondent has established a prima facie case, supported by materials indicating prior commercial use of the ‘Brahmins’ trade mark. The balance of convenience is also in favour of the respondent. If the impugned use is ultimately found to infringe the respondent’s [Wipro] rights, its continued use may erode the distinctiveness of the trade mark and cause injury not readily compensable in damages. These conclusions are tentative and shall not prejudice the final adjudication of the suit, " the Court said in its judgment.
